lead: St. Petersburg plumbing deals with heat, storm surge, old cast-iron drains and 1920s homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across St. Pete.
risk: cast-iron drain failures, slab leaks and storm-surge flooding
risk_short: cast-iron drains, slab leaks and flooding
why: Old Northeast, Kenwood and Crescent Lake have homes from the 1920s, with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Many mid-century homes have cast-iron drains under the slab that are rotting from the inside.
Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024 flooded thousands of homes with surge water. Flooded homes can have hidden damage in drains, water heaters and gas controls.
utility: City of St. Petersburg Water Resources
water: St. Petersburg buys most of its water from Tampa Bay Water, which blends groundwater, river water and desalinated seawater. It is moderately hard.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Have a plumber check the water heater after any flood.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown, Old Northeast, Kenwood, Crescent Lake, Snell Isle, Shore Acres, Old Southeast and every other St. Petersburg neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of St. Petersburg Construction Services and Permitting, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: What plumbing checks should St. Pete homes get after storm surge?
faq.a: Have the water heater, gas lines and sewer line checked before regular use. Salt water ruins heater controls, and silt clogs drains. Keep photos and receipts for your insurance claim.
